title: Scientists built a camera that can track invisible particles in 3D
hook: A new detector called PLATON swaps millions of wired-together sensor parts for one solid light-emitting block, read out by a camera and AI — and it may sharpen medical scans too.
key_points: PLATON is a new particle detector that could replace millions of tiny detector components.
It uses a single block of light-producing material instead of wiring together separate elements.
A light-field camera and highly sensitive photon sensors capture the light it emits.
AI reconstructs particle paths from that data in fast, detailed 3D.
Simulations suggest it could match or beat today's best detectors while being far easier to scale.
The same technology may also lead to sharper PET medical scans.
content_html: According to a ScienceDaily report, scientists have built a new particle detector called PLATON that could replace millions of tiny detector components with a single block of light-producing material. A light-field camera and highly sensitive photon sensors capture the light it emits, and AI reconstructs particle paths in fast, detailed 3D.
extra_html: Simulations suggest PLATON could match or surpass today's best particle detectors while being far easier to scale, since it swaps a tangle of wired components for one solid block. Researchers say the same approach may also lead to sharper PET scans in medicine.

related.title: Catching the Ghost Particle
related.hook: Trillions of neutrinos stream through your body every second, yet they almost never touch anything. To catch even a few, physicists build some of the most audacious detectors ever conceived.

related.title: A Single Laser Shot Now Images Through 15 Meters of Lead
related.hook: Muon imaging usually means waiting hours for enough cosmic-ray muons to trickle through. A laser-driven muon beam just did the same job — through a truck and a building wall — in a single shot.
